prize_parts.citation: for methods to estimate demand and competition in differentiated-product markets with endogenous prices

statement.case_for: My laureates stay the same as in round 1, with a narrower citation. B047 is a well-bounded discovery with a compact, traceable credit core: Berry (1994) and Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes (1995) solved the problem of recovering substitution patterns and markups when prices are endogenous and products are differentiated. The framework has been used for about thirty years in merger review, antitrust, regulation, auctions, trade and health. The chair asked whether this is industrial organisation or econometric methodology. I see it as both. It makes a substantive quantity (demand and market power) measurable under explicit identifying assumptions, and that is the kind of measurement advance I value from my own field. Pakes' dynamic-industry work is part of why he belongs among the three. I now word the citation around demand estimation with endogenous prices. Hjalmarsson and Stromberg argue that a narrow, paper-anchored citation keeps the credit defensible, and I find that persuasive. A citation covering dynamic games would invite the Benkard-Levin and Bresnahan-Reiss questions that the three-name cap cannot answer. Answering the chair's question on B006: a two-name Kiyotaki-Moore prize would not become my first preference. The criterion that keeps B047 ahead is the more settled empirical and applied record together with the cleaner attribution. I do not rely on the 2022 adjacency, which I discuss below. I regard the gap as narrow.
statement.case_against: The three-name cap leaves out Bresnahan and Reiss, whose entry and market-structure work is an earlier and distinct tradition, and Benkard and Levin on dynamic estimation. Under a demand-estimation citation that cost is acceptable to me, but it is real, and a Committee that wanted to honour structural IO as a whole would see it as a defect. Counterfactual markups and merger predictions depend on functional-form and equilibrium assumptions, and a body of work that is a method may be judged against one that is a mechanism. Pakes' share is arguably larger than the other two names' shares, as Stromberg notes. B047 also starts with fewer opening first-place rankings than B006 and without a majority. I do not treat that as evidence about merit, but it means this may be a minority judgement. On the chair's question about the 2022 prize, I do not think thematic adjacency should count much against B006. The collateral-amplification mechanism is a different discovery from bank-run and deposit-insurance theory. That weakens one of the reasons I might have given for ranking B047 first, and I am dropping it. The same standard applies to B023, whose overlap with the 2021, 2023 and 2024 prizes matters only to the extent that the same discovery was already credited.

responses.point: In his own round-1 file the chair proposes three names for B006 (Kiyotaki, Moore, Gertler). He moved from two names because Gertler's intermediary-frictions work with Kiyotaki extends collateral constraints to banks and is separate from the Bernanke-Gertler accelerator. He wants the citation to exclude the accelerator and the bank-run themes of the 2022 prize.
responses.response: My round-1 reply addressed a two-name Kiyotaki-Moore proposal, and the chair's summary correctly notes that this misdescribed his current file, so I restate my response. His reasoning is stronger than the two-name argument I answered. If the Gertler-Kiyotaki intermediary papers are a separable achievement, the third name is defensible and a citation anchored on collateral and balance-sheet amplification handles the overlap concern. I cannot verify from the supplied evidence how much of that credit is independent of the accelerator line, and I would want that checked. B006 in either form remains my strongest alternative. It does not change my first choice, because I give more weight to B047's more settled empirical record and cleaner attribution core.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B006 first and B047 second. He argues that collateral and financial-friction mechanisms are now part of the shared core of macro, finance and policy modelling, while BLP is a toolkit concentrated in IO and adjacent applied fields. He also says a mechanism need not be settled in every empirical detail to be prize-worthy if it organised a large research programme and passed the 2008 test.
responses.response: I accept the principle that a mechanism does not need every empirical detail settled, and I would not hold B006 to a stricter standard than I hold B047, whose counterfactuals are also model-dependent. I weigh the criterion of breadth differently. BLP's use extends beyond IO into trade, health, environmental economics and regulatory practice, and those are settings where the estimates are checked against outcomes such as merger retrospectives. This is a judgement about weight, and I do not claim it is decisive. Because the Committee has no majority, I would rather leave this disagreement open than blur it.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B047 first with the same three names. She argues that the three-name core is compact and traceable to specific papers, and that the Bresnahan-Reiss and dynamic-games lines are separable achievements that would turn a clean trio into a contested five- or seven-person award. She also says assumption-dependence is real but the assumptions are explicit and routinely probed.
responses.response: I agree and have adopted her narrower citation, with demand estimation and endogenous prices at its centre. That is my main change from round 1, when my citation also covered dynamic industries. I would add one caution to her validation point. Sensitivity analysis and merger retrospectives address assumption-dependence only in part, and the Committee should not treat the record as stronger than it is. I take her point that this is an argument about how openly the identifying assumptions are stated, not that they are innocuous.

responses.point: Dreber ranks B023 first with Autor, Hanson and Dorn. She argues that the China-shock papers are a jointly authored core with one design and one data source, and that a citation anchored in empirical analyses of labour demand and local adjustment avoids claiming the task-model theory that partly sits with Acemoglu and Restrepo.
responses.response: This narrowing answers the bundling objection that led me to rank B023 eighth in round 1. An Autor-Dorn-Hanson trade-shock citation has a clearer single-discovery logic than the three-strand bundle, and it keeps Dorn, a co-originator. Because of this I replace B036 with B023 as my second alternative. The attribution problems raised for B036 by Hjalmarsson, Stromberg and Hassler (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum, Yeaple outside the credited names) are not resolved by the cap. The remaining concerns about B023 are the persistence and magnitude of the local effects and the shift-share inference, which Dreber herself flags. I still place it behind B047 on attribution clarity and the settled evidence.

responses.point: Stromberg ranks B047 first and wants a narrow citation for the demand-estimation and dynamic-industry methods, not the whole empirical-IO tradition. He notes that Pakes' share is arguably larger than the other two names' shares, so the attribution is less symmetrical than it looks.
responses.response: I agree that the Committee should say openly that the citation is for estimation methods and not for structural IO as a whole. The asymmetry of Pakes' share is a fair point, and I do not think it undermines the trio. Berry (1994) and BLP (1995) are separate identifiable papers, and the Committee can acknowledge different shares without splitting the credit differently. If members regard the asymmetry as serious, the alternative is to keep the citation on demand estimation and not widen the group, as he and Hjalmarsson suggest.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee reads B047 as industrial organisation or as econometric methodology, and how it compares with foundational mechanisms such as B006.
Whether the omission of Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin is acceptable under a demand-estimation citation, or is seen as a defect of the cap.

Whether Gertler's intermediary-frictions work with Kiyotaki is separable from the Bernanke-Gertler accelerator. I cannot assess this from the supplied evidence, and it decides whether B006 is a two-name or three-name prize.
How large and persistent the China-shock effects are, which bears on my second alternative B023.
My assessments rely on general knowledge of the literatures, not on verified citation, usage or attribution data. I see no majority in round 1, so I may hold a minority view.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to B047, B006 or B023 or their credited names is apparent from my profile. I disclose that B021 is a different case: my profile lists a corruption paper co-authored with Persson and Rothstein and long-standing work close to that literature, and I delivered the 2024 presentation speech on institutions. This is one reason B021 is neither my preferred configuration nor an alternative. I also note that I am a Stockholm University colleague, in a different department, of committee members Hassler, Krusell and Boppart (IIES). Disclosed, not adjudicated.
